lesson.subtitle: Lesson 19 -- Do You Know Him? The People of the Trip: Me, Him, Her, Them
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Leão | Lesson 19 -- Do You Know Him?
lesson.grammar_point: object pronouns me, him, her, us, them

listenings.text: Five years ago, I was on a train from Paris to Amsterdam. There was a woman next to me, a stranger, and she had a big map of the city. I asked her: are you going to Amsterdam for the first time? She looked at me and smiled. We talked for four hours. Her name was Ana, from Chile. At the station I gave her my number, and she gave me hers. That night we had dinner together. Now she is my best friend. I visit her in Chile, and she visits me in London. And it all started with one question to a stranger.

I travel a lot, so I miss my family. My daughter calls me every night, and I tell her about the city. My son is fourteen, so he doesn't call me. I call him, and he answers with one word. My wife sends me photos of them every morning, the two kids at breakfast. When I come home, I always bring them something small. Last time I bought my daughter a book, and I bought my son a T-shirt. He didn't say thank you, but he wears it every day. So I think he likes it.

extra_audio.text: Claire, the man in the blue shirt... I remember him. That is Paul. You met him in Rome. And the couple at the end of the table? They are the Millers. Do you know them? No, I don't. Can you introduce me to them?
